added_models.model: AD-patient-derived cortical-neuron secreted tau (eTau) neutralization: primary human neurons and two human-tau transgenic mouse lines (iPierian)

engagement.model: AD-patient-derived cortical-neuron eTau in human neurons and two human-tau transgenic mouse lines
engagement.note: IPN002's lineage antibodies neutralized eTau purified from AD-patient neuron media, lowering Abeta in human neurons and two human-tau mouse lines; no human Abeta readout yet.
engagement.short: eTau neutralization lowers Abeta in model
engagement.quote: We found that neutralizing eTau reduces Aβ levels in vitro in primary human cortical neurons where exogenously adding eTau increases Aβ levels.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Elsevier paywall, no PMC copy): the abstract names neither the two human-tau transgenic lines nor the antibody clone; Courade 2018 identifies antibody A (WO2014028777A2, IPN002) as the antibody 'developed to bind an N-terminal fragment of Tau hypothesized to potentiate beta amyloid accumulation [3]', citing this paper.
engagement.judgement: Separate track under the run's identity rule: patient-derived eTau in human neurons with an Abeta readout is a different system from the P301 mice and makes a different prediction (Abeta falls when eTau is neutralized). The in-vivo arm's mouse lines are unverified, so the track is named by its distinctive patient-derived component.

engagement.model: AD-patient-derived cortical-neuron eTau in human neurons and two human-tau transgenic mouse lines
engagement.note: Gosuranemab cut CSF unbound N-terminal tau at every dose, yet week-76 CSF Abeta42 moved no more than placebo (-1.90% high dose vs -3.81%).
engagement.short: CSF Abeta42 unchanged despite tau capture
engagement.quote: Levels of the amyloid-β isoform Aβ42 in the CSF were also measured, and the changes from baseline at week 76 were small and comparable between groups
engagement.confidence_note: Paired comparison: Shulman 2023 (PMC10724064, full text read) reports CSF Abeta42 but cites neither Bright 2015 nor the eTau-to-Abeta hypothesis; the Abeta42 readout is not among the outcomes posted on the registry (2022-11-08), so the comparison dates to the paper. The model side is read at abstract level.
engagement.reason: Abeta did not fall as eTau model predicted
engagement.judgement: The model's stated prediction was that neutralizing eTau lowers Abeta. In TANGO the antibody removed unbound N-terminal tau from CSF at all doses (P < 0.0001) but Abeta42 did not change against placebo (-8.99 pg/ml, -1.90%, high dose; -17.38 pg/ml, -3.81%, placebo), so the downstream readout the model used did not move: contra, readout downstream. product_in_model false: Bright used the IPN002 lineage, not the humanized product. The N-terminal-tau readout itself is the existing mouse track's and is not re-scored here.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of Abeta change: model predicted a fall, CSF Abeta42 change indistinguishable from placebo

added_models.model: P301S mouse-brain-lysate tau seeding biosensor assay (HEK293 RD(dK280)-CFP/YFP FRET cells; WashU/Diamond)

efficacy.model: P301S mouse-brain-lysate tau seeding biosensor assay (HEK293 FRET cells)
efficacy.note: HJ8.5, tilavonemab's parent, was selected because it blocked P301S-lysate seeding at 0.25 ug/ml, the most potent of the panel; no patient result existed.
efficacy.short: HJ8.5 picked for blocking mouse seeds
efficacy.quote: Using a cell-based biosensor assay, we screened anti-tau monoclonal antibodies for their ability to block seeding activity present in P301S brain lysates.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3924573 author manuscript via NCBI efetch).
efficacy.judgement: Separate track under the run's identity rule: the mouse-seed counterpart of Courade's AD-seed assay, a different seed source that made the opposite prediction for the same V-region (full blockade here; 'partial activity against AD-PHF Tau' only at the highest doses as antibody B in Courade 2018). Its in-vivo arm (HJ8.5 infused into P301S mice) stays on the tau-tg-mice-p301 track. Own data: 'The HJ8.5 antibody blocked seeding activity at concentrations as low as 0.25 μg/ml compared to controls.'

efficacy.model: P301S mouse-brain-lysate tau seeding biosensor assay (HEK293 FRET cells)
efficacy.note: Tilavonemab, humanized HJ8.5, missed CDR-SB at 300-2000 mg in 453 early AD patients; the mouse-seed assay had ranked HJ8.5 the most potent seed blocker.
efficacy.short: Mouse-seed blocker failed in early AD
efficacy.quote: Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer's disease.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired comparison (Florian 2023 does not cite Yanamandra 2013 as a prediction); patient side read at abstract level; registry results posting 2022-08-26 is the earliest both sides were public.
efficacy.reason: Blocked mouse seeds; no clinical effect
efficacy.judgement: Courade 2018 had already found the same V-region (antibody B) 'demonstrated partial activity against AD-PHF Tau, neutralizing seeding activity by 74%' and only 'abruptly and only at the highest doses tested', so the two seed sources disagreed before the trial and the AD seeds were right. Primary endpoint CDR-SB (registry confirmed). Tilavonemab's 2019 PSP failure (Hoglinger 2021) is another indication and is not scored here.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of seeding blockade vs clinical change

patient_trials.quote: Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer's disease.

added_models.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, transgenic-mouse ISF and patient CSF, read in tau biosensor cells and mouse primary neurons (Biogen)

engagement.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
engagement.note: The product itself depleted unbound N-terminal tau from PSP and AD patient CSF ex vivo and removed seeding-competent tau from AD brain homogenate.
engagement.short: Ex-vivo CSF and AD-lysate depletion assays
engagement.quote: Immunodepletion of pathological human brain homogenates and transgenic mouse interstitial fluid (ISF) with gosuranemab resulted in reduced tau aggregation in tau biosensor cells.
engagement.judgement: Opens the sponsor's own ex-vivo track at first publication; the humanized product, not a murine parent, was used (product_in_model true).

engagement.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
engagement.note: Ex-vivo depletion of unbound N-terminal tau in PSP/AD patient CSF matched the >90% CSF suppression seen in dosed cohorts.
engagement.short: Ex-vivo CSF depletion matched clinical CSF engagement
engagement.quote: These results are consistent with the >90% target engagement observed in the CSF of some clinical trial dosing cohorts and support the evaluation of gosuranemab as a potential treatment for AD.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The paper postdates the clinical CSF data it cites (Qureshi 2018 healthy volunteers 67-97%; Boxer 2019 PSP 90-96%); whether the ex-vivo CSF experiment was run before those readouts is not stated, so a checker may rule this a retrodiction.
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison in the model paper itself: ex-vivo depletion of unbound N-terminal tau in patient CSF against the dosed cohorts' CSF suppression. Readout direct (free target). subjects mixed: healthy volunteers (phase 1) and PSP patients; AD patients' CSF engagement followed in TANGO (Shulman 2023, all doses P < 0.0001). Scored same rather than retro because the ex-vivo unbound-tau assay is the bench form of the clinical PD assay and plausibly preceded it; flagged low confidence.
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction and extent of unbound N-terminal tau depletion (ex-vivo patient CSF vs dosed-cohort CSF, >90%)

efficacy.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
efficacy.note: Gosuranemab removed seeding-competent tau from AD brain homogenate and blocked AD-tau seeding in mouse primary neurons; TANGO had not read out.
efficacy.short: Product neutralizes AD seeds ex vivo
efficacy.quote: Preincubation of seed-competent AD-tau with gosuranemab significantly inhibited tau aggregation in mouse primary cortical neurons.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from Courade's ad-tau-seeding-assay under the run's identity rule: a different procedure (immunodepletion of homogenate, primary-neuron seeding, the humanized product rather than a mouse-IgG1 V-region graft) that made the opposite prediction for the same antibody (active here; 'essentially inactive' as antibody A there). If a checker treats the two AD-seed systems as one, these entries fold into that track as its own-data conflict.

efficacy.model: Gosuranemab immunodepletion of AD/PSP brain homogenate, mouse ISF and patient CSF (biosensor cells, primary neurons)
efficacy.note: Shulman names the AD-lysate and ISF depletion data as TANGO's preclinical basis; no dose changed CDR-SB at week 78.
efficacy.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10724064); the model side is read at abstract level.
efficacy.reason: Seed removal ex vivo; CDR-SB unmoved
efficacy.judgement: Stated comparison: Shulman 2023 writes 'This study is supported by preclinical data demonstrating the high binding affinity of gosuranemab to monomeric and aggregated forms of tau and its ability to remove seeding-competent forms of tau from AD brain lysate' (citing Sopko 2020 as ref 18) and then reports no CDR-SB effect at any dose; the authors' explanation is that 'targeting an N-terminal tau epitope may not sufficiently capture extracellular tau species responsible for mediating tau pathology propagation'. TANGO's registry primary is safety with CDR-SB the powered efficacy gate (poc_gate). Year is the paper's, the first time the model side was put beside the result; the registry posting (2022-11-08) carries no model side.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of seed removal vs clinical change

patient_trials.quote: No significant effects were identified in cognitive and functional tests as no dose resulted in a favorable change from the baseline CDR-SB score at week 78 compared to placebo control

added_models.model: Certara QSP model of synaptic-cleft tau secretion, antibody capture and postsynaptic uptake coupled to a PBPK model (Geerts 2023); spatial Monte Carlo successor (Goff 2025)

efficacy.model: QSP model of synaptic-cleft tau secretion, antibody capture and uptake, coupled to PBPK
efficacy.note: ODE model of secretion, antibody capture and uptake in the synaptic cleft with PBPK-derived CSF/ISF exposure, built to simulate the gosuranemab, tilavonemab and semorinemab trials.
efficacy.short: QSP cleft model built after failures
efficacy.quote: Integration with a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model allowed us to simulate clinical trials of anti-tau antibodies gosuranemab, tilavonemab, semorinemab, and anti-aSyn antibodies cinpanemab and prasineuzumab.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the model was built after the Tauriel (2022) and the gosuranemab and tilavonemab PSP (2021) failures were public. Separate in-silico track: a different system from the mice and the seeding assays, built to explain rather than to select.

efficacy.model: QSP model of synaptic-cleft tau secretion, antibody capture and uptake, coupled to PBPK
efficacy.note: Simulated 45-99% CSF engagement but 1-3% in the cleft, cutting oligomeric-tau uptake by under 1% even at 8100 mg; reproduces semorinemab's Tauriel miss.
efficacy.quote: On the other hand, due to the avid binding of oligomeric tau to postsynaptic receptors, gosuranemab maximally reduces the uptake of oligomeric tau by 0.008%.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. For the AD context the member patient datum the paper simulates is semorinemab's Tauriel (Teng 2022); gosuranemab and tilavonemab are simulated against their PSP trials, and the paper notes gosuranemab's AD data were unreported when it was written. Senior author Courade is the UCB antibody-D author (Courade 2018).
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): parameterized from the members' phase 1 PK and run after the phase 2 outcomes were known, so it reproduces rather than predicts: 'retro', never 'same'. The comparison is stated in the paper ('Both tilavonemab in progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) and semorinemab in AD failed to change clinical progression', with the simulations beside them). Its CSF-engagement figures are fitted to the observed CSF data, so no engagement entry is scored.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction: simulated <1% reduction in oligomeric-tau uptake vs no clinical effect

patient_trials.quote: semorinemab did not slow clinical AD progression compared with placebo throughout the 73-week study period

efficacy.model: Spatial Monte Carlo (MCell) model of antibody and tau trajectories in the synaptic cleft
efficacy.note: Spatial Monte Carlo of the cleft: under 0.5% of ISF antibody enters and seed uptake falls under 10%, using the same three members' parameters.
efficacy.quote: These simulations using a detailed and realistic biological environment provide a possible explanation for the clinical trial failures of anti-tau and anti-αsynuclein antibodies.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12256572). Antibody parameters are those of semorinemab, tilavonemab and gosuranemab; the paper names no trial endpoint, the failures are cited (Teng 2022, Hoglinger 2021, Dam 2021).
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction by the same group with a different numerical method and the same conclusion; kept on the QSP track as a strengthening entry because it makes the same prediction. Its own account of the 2023 model: 'This model was able to provide a rationale for the observed clinical trial failures of three different antibodies (gosuranemab, tilavonemab and semorinemab) tested at very high doses (up to 120 mg/kg).'
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction: simulated <10% reduction in seed uptake vs no clinical effect

patient_trials.quote: semorinemab did not slow clinical AD progression compared with placebo throughout the 73-week study period

considered_not_added: Yanamandra 2017 (HJ8.5 in P301S mice beside ABBV-8E12 plasma tau in PSP patients, stated): the existing tau-tg-mice-p301 track; it is a dating correction (engagement same 2017) for the draft, not a new system.

Qureshi 2018 (gosuranemab in healthy volunteers, CSF unbound N-terminal tau suppressed 67-97%) paired with the mouse-ISF N-terminal-tau removal (Bright 2015 in-vivo arm; Sopko 2020 treated transgenic mice): the ISF-to-CSF N-terminal tau readout is the existing mouse track's, so no new track; the ex-vivo patient-CSF version of that readout is scored on the Sopko track instead.

Bright 2015 eTau model, efficacy cell: not added. The model's distinctive claim is the Abeta mechanism (scored as engagement, downstream); the CDR-SB failure is already scored against gosuranemab's own stated preclinical basis (Sopko track) and the mouse track, and a third entry would count one trial three times.
Goff 2025 spatial Monte Carlo model of the synaptic cleft: added as a strengthening entry on the QSP track rather than its own track (same group, same three member antibodies, same prediction).
Geerts 2023 QSP model, engagement cell: its simulated CSF engagement (45% semorinemab to 99% gosuranemab) is fitted to the observed phase 1 CSF data, not a prediction; not scored.

PSP trials of gosuranemab (Boxer 2019 phase 1b; Dam 2021 PASSPORT) and tilavonemab (Hoglinger 2021): another indication's patients, not a model system; safety would be importable (imported_from PSP) but no model safety prediction exists to compare it with.
Courade 2018 antibody F (zagotenemab's MC-1 V-region, 'showed only partial activity on AD Tau'): belongs to the existing ad-tau-seeding-assay track (checker's own note), not a new system.

Alternative reading of Sopko 2020 vs Courade 2018: both use AD-brain-derived seeds in a cell assay. Kept separate under the run's identity rule (different procedure and product form, opposite prediction for the same antibody); if a checker treats them as one AD-seed system, the Sopko entries fold into ad-tau-seeding-assay as its own-data conflict.
Tau-PET stratification (zagotenemab's intermediate tau-PET entry criterion) and plasma p-tau: patient-selection biomarkers, not model systems.
Semorinemab exposure model behind the 4500 mg arm (Teng 2022): unpublished and already in the draft's dose cell on the mouse track.

Patient-derived iPSC neurons or organoids dosed with anti-tau antibodies: the Europe PMC search returned reviews only, no patient comparison; the hiPSC-neuron tau-uptake data in Geerts 2023 are calibration inputs, not a track.
Human genetic models (MAPT mutation carriers, H1/H2 haplotype): no anti-MAPT antibody patient comparison in AD.
Biogen press release 2021-06-16 (TANGO discontinuation, tier 5): a dating question on the existing tracks, not a model system; not cited here.
Cynomolgus PK/PD (Ayalon 2021): the existing nhp-pkpd safety track.
